articles.title_orig: Ilhan Omar Investigation Aims to Build Case for Stripping Her Citizenship
articles.title_zh: Ilhan Omar Investigation Aims to Build Case for Stripping Her Citizenship
articles.content_orig:
Rep. Ilhan Omar, a Democrat from Minnesota, during a news conference at the US Capitol on Feb. 24, 2026, in Washington, D.C.
In a highly unusual step, federal agents this week aggressively intensified their investigations into Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, weeks before she stands for reelection in her home district.
The Department of Justice on Tuesday subpoenaed relatives of Omar’s family members, including her sister Sahra Noor, according to The New York Times . The grand jury subpoenas were issued shortly after a raid of the lawmaker’s residence in Washington, D.C. on Monday.
The judicial search warrant, which is under seal, was executed by Homeland Security Investigations, the investigative branch of Immigration and Customs Enforcement . Although the Department of Justice did not provide any more details of the investigation, multiple outlets , citing anonymous sources, reported that the search stemmed from Omar’s immigration paperwork, which was filled out by her late father when she was a child.
Prior to the investigation, multiple Trump Administration officials have accused Omar of immigration fraud without presenting any evidence. In a podcast interview in March, Vice President JD Vance said the White House was exploring “legal remedies” to her alleged immigration fraud. Last month, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the investigation into Omar was “ongoing” and dismissed efforts to frame the case as political retribution.
“If we actually move a case forward, it’s not a political case. It's actually a case because they did things wrong,” Mullin said during the interview with right-wing podcaster Benny Johnson.
Omar, who has long denied the allegations, condemned the raid on her home as “political intimidation” and said she will “not be silenced.”
President Trump, along with many MAGA Republicans, has repeatedly floated the idea of revoking Omar’s citizenship, a process also known as denaturalization, and deporting her.
But legal and immigration experts tell TIME that denaturalizing a U.S. citizen is a rare and difficult process, one that requires federal authorities to clear a high bar in front of a federal judge. Here’s what to know about how the process works.
Stripping someone of their citizenship is a more arduous legal process than most other immigration efforts that involve the courts. Deportation proceedings, for instance, are initiated by ICE agents under the Department of Homeland Security and are then approved by immigration judges who are hired and work within the Department of Justice. The denaturalization process, on the other hand, must be approved by an independent federal judge, who evaluates the request by a higher standard.
All denaturalization efforts begin at DOJ. In order to revoke a naturalized person’s citizenship, a DOJ lawyer must decide whether to file a civil or a criminal petition in court. Yuripzy Morgan, an attorney and host of Free Range National podcase, said a civil complaint does not have a statute of limitation, whereas a criminal complaint has a statute of limitation of 10 years and must clear a much higher legal bar.
“For civil denaturalization, the government has to show that there is clear, convincing, and unequivocal evidence that the person in question obtained their naturalization either illegally, or they willfully misrepresented a material fact, ” Morgan says. She stressed that simply having an error in an immigration document doesn't mean that a judge is going to approve stripping a person of their citizenship.
For a criminal denaturalization conviction, the federal government must show “proof beyond a reasonable doubt” that the individual knowingly obtained citizenship through fraud, which is the highest legal standard of proof required to secure a criminal conviction. In 2017, the Supreme Court unanimously ruled in Maslenjak v. United States that only an illegal act that played a role in a person’s citizenship application could lead to criminal denaturalization, further narrowing down the scope of such efforts.
Omar’s father filled out and submitted her citizenship application on her behalf when she was 17. It is unclear what evidence, if any, the federal government has to show that anything in the application was fraudulent, or that Omar or her father intentionally misrepresented anything in that application.
Andrew Arthur, a former immigration judge and a resident fellow at the Center for Immigration Studies, pointed out that even after someone gets denaturalized, a deportation is not guaranteed. The person would still be able to retain their previous legal immigration status until a final order of removal is issued to the person by ICE.
“If they had a green card before they naturalized, even after they get denaturalized, they are going to have a green card,” Arthur says.
According to Omar’s House biography, Omar and her family fled her home country Somalia when she was eight. The family eventually sought asylum in the United States in 1995. She told The New York Times that she became a U.S. citizen in 2000 when she was 17.
At the time Omar went through the process, federal law allowed immigrants under the age of 18 to get naturalized as U.S. citizens if both of their parents had become U.S. citizens. The law was eventually replaced by a new law in 2001, which only requires one parent to become a citizen for the children to be naturalized.
At the center of this investigation is whether Omar’s father, Nur Omar Mohamed, lied about her age in immigration documents so she could be eligible to derive citizenship through him, according to The Washington Post , which cited two unnamed sources.
According to Arthur, the former immigration judge, if Omar was 18 at the time of the naturalization application, she may have been able to apply for her citizenship on her own after having a valid green card for five years.
The allegations regarding Omar’s citizenship gained attention among conservative activists and commentators starting in 2019, when Omar became a member of Congress. Shortly after her election, Omar’s staff sought to change her official birth year in public records from 1981 to 1982, according to multiple outlets .
Despite the renewed push from the second Trump administration, denaturalization remains an exceedingly rare legal process. According to the Migration Policy Institute , a Washington, D.C.-based think tank, an average of 11 denaturalization cases were filed per year between 1990 and 2017.
Denaturalization efforts have increased in Trump’s second term. The DOJ has announced efforts to strip at least 108 people of their citizenship in 2026. That is still considerably smaller than the hundreds of thousands of people whom the U.S. government grants citizenship to through naturalization every year.

articles.title_orig: Ilhan Omar’s phone seized and relatives subpoenaed in criminal inquiry, source says
articles.title_zh: Ilhan Omar’s phone seized and relatives subpoenaed in criminal inquiry, source says
articles.content_orig:
Federal authorities issued more than a dozen grand jury subpoenas in inquiry into potential immigration fraud
US politics live – latest updates
Federal authorities investigating the Minnesota representative Ilhan Omar seized the Democratic lawmaker’s phone and have issued more than a dozen grand jury subpoenas, including to some of her relatives, according to a person briefed on the inquiry.
The subpoenas were issued for a grand jury collecting evidence in Minnesota as federal authorities investigate potential fraud in Omar’s immigration paperwork, said the person, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss an ongoing investigation. The investigation led to federal agents searching Omar’s Washington DC home on Monday just weeks before the November midterms , in which Omar is seeking re-election.
The scope of the investigation into Omar is unclear, though the secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, Markwayne Mullin, has suggested that authorities were examining potential crimes related to her family’s immigration paperwork.
On Tuesday, Jeanine Pirro, the US attorney for the District of Columbia, said in a Fox News interview that “there are several investigations going on” related to Omar and that her office is also looking into issues concerning the lawmaker’s financial disclosures.
“If there was a crime that was committed, it will be prosecuted,” Pirro said.
The search of Omar’s home so close to next month’s midterm contests, which will determine control of the House and the Senate, was swiftly condemned by Democrats, who accused the administration of targeting the representative for political purposes. Omar, in a statement on X, called the search an “attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement”.
“For 10 years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation,” she said. “I will not be silenced.”
A phone message seeking comment was left on Wednesday with a representative for Omar.
after newsletter promotion
Though the Republican focus on Omar’s background dates back years, the search notably took place three weeks before the November midterms, in which Omar is seeking re-election. The justice department has historically sought to avoid public investigative actions involving a candidate within 60 days of a primary or general election.
Omar, who was first elected to the House in 2018, represents Minnesota’s fifth district, including Minneapolis. She is part of “the Squad” of progressive lawmakers who are a vibrant political force on the left wing of Congress but have also endured repeated attacks from Trump, dating back to his first term. She was one of the first two Muslim American women in the House and the first African refugee to be elected to Congress.

articles.title_zh: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird
articles.content_orig:
On a rainy Wednesday afternoon, a novelty toy and games store in a quiet part of New York City was seeing much busier foot traffic than usual.
Inside, the shop was packed with cameramen and customers, while passersby in this Brooklyn neighbourhood of Cobble Hill looked inside, asking: "Where's the bird?"
Art of Play has found itself at the centre of a social media storm since the weekend when Grammy-winning musician Kelly Clarkson complained online that the boutique store would not let her buy a singing and dancing mechanical bird that was perched on the wall.
The Since U Been Gone singer claimed she was "looked at as if I couldn't afford" the bird - which she said had a price tag of $15,000 (£11,000).
"Y'all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts' character in Pretty Woman," she said, referring to a scene from the 1990 romantic comedy film where Roberts' character is treated poorly by staff at a  shop, who imply she cannot afford various items.
In a follow-up post on social media, Clarkson said the store had told her the bird cost $15,000 and that they could find her something else "comparable".
Art of Play has defended how it treated the star on social media, saying the wooden bird - which is called Molly - is permanently attached to the wall and is not for sale.
It said that during Clarkson's five-minute visit on Saturday, an employee suggested to her that she could buy an identical bird for $15,000.
They also said they had offered her a different singing bird for $2,000 from a clock-making shop in Germany, which she could have purchased that day.
"Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by eight million people who have never visited our store," Art of Play said.
"It's been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity."
Clarkson defended her decision to criticise the store on social media, saying: "I never blast people but you my friend were an exception."
When the BBC visited the store on Wednesday, there were more reporters than customers.
A shopkeeper said they would not comment on the story anymore and just wanted to get back to business as usual.
Molly still hung on the wall at the shop, this time next to a price tag of $15m.
The sign jokes that the sculpture is the "world's most famous singing bird automata!"
The store's owner has said he and his staff have faced threats and harassment after Clarkson's complaint, telling the BBC's US partner CBS News that the singer had endangered them.
This week, a man filmed himself yelling expletives outside the store, before accusing its employees of "racially profiling" Clarkson.
The kerfuffle lingered in headlines on Wednesday as a news outlet released surveillance video from Art of Play purporting to show Clarkson's visit.
The grainy footage, which has no audio, is said to show her wearing a yellow shirt, a baseball cap and a backpack while browsing items, including Molly the bird.
She can be seen talking with an employee - apparently about the bird as she points at it - and later moving to leave the store. She comes back in to say something animatedly to the cashier.
But while the argument over the bird has gone viral online, some of Art of Play's customers had not heard about it before being greeted by news cameras on the premises.
One customer who was in town visiting his daughter said he was not familiar with the controversy.
For others, Clarkson's claims that those at the store had treated her rudely came as a surprise.
Kiran Ramineni, who lives next door, described Art of Play as a "very nice small mom and pop store" and said he had seen flocks of journalists there in recent days.
Shopgoer Emily Trantanella, 27, said: "I feel like a pretty woman and I've always been treated very well here.

articles.title_orig: Mary Cassatt exhibit at Art Institute aims to recreate lost mural from 1893 World's Fair
articles.title_zh: Mary Cassatt exhibit at Art Institute aims to recreate lost mural from 1893 World's Fair
articles.content_orig:
The 1893 World's Fair looms large in Chicago history.
Now, one of its groundbreaking works of art is a centerpiece of a new exhibit at the Art Institute of Chicago — but there is one big problem.
At the heart of this exhibit at the Art Institute is a work that no longer exists.
"It's a tough problem for a curator to have, to center this story about a monumental mural without the mural," said Annelise Madsen with the Art Institute.
That mural, " Modern Woman " by Mary Cassatt, was from the 1893 World's Fair.
"It was Cassatt really scaling up her subject matter, what she had built her career portraying, the lives of everyday women, but giving that a sense of import, a sense of grandeur," Madsen said.
Cassatt now has her own exhibit at the Art Institute, which aims to recreate the form and spirit of the long-lost mural.
"What we do have are a lot of enticing traces," Madsen said. "We have archival material. We have reproductions of the mural that are in fair publications from the 1890s. We have letters by Cassatt."
The exhibit covers a lifetime of Cassatt's work beyond the missing mural — like the iconic painting, "The Child's Bath," from 1893.
"She was a fierce, independent woman and an artist of the time," Madsen said. "I think she was, first of all, showing us the impact of human connection."
Her impact still felt, even through a mural that we can't see.
"It's a Chicago story, and we, for that reason alone, we must embrace it. It's part of the history of this city."
Mary Cassatt actually helped the art institute get one of its signature works — El Greco's " The Assumption of the Virgin ."
In 1905, Cassatt wrote to the institute's president when the painting became available, saying it belonged there.
Cassatt's exhibit runs through January 3, 2027.

A global sell-off in memory-chip stocks deepened overnight as South Korea's benchmark KOSPI ( ^KS11 ) tanked 7%.
Micron ( MU ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) were poised to open lower on Wednesday as SK Hynix ( 000660.KS ) and Samsung Electronics ( 005930.KS ) fell 10% and 8%, respectively, after tanking earlier this week over concerns about intensifying competition from China. The two memory giants account for more than half of the South Korean stock market's total capitalization.
The sell-off in South Korea followed a decline in the chip sector on Wall Street on Wednesday as worries about further rate hikes collided with fears of AI-driven debt financing.
Chip giant Nvidia ( NVDA ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), AMD ( AMD ), and Intel ( INTC ) all led the chip stocks lower during the session.
On Wednesday, worries about borrowing costs also hit the AI trade.
CoreWeave ( CRWV ) stock fell more than 15% after a chart of the neocloud providers' bond yields circulated on social media.
The stock's sharp sell-off highlighted concerns about the company's debt-heavy balance sheet and whether it can scale fast enough to manage its growing interest expense.
Any slowdown in AI spending could spell trouble for chip makers, which have been the main beneficiaries of infrastructure spending as hyperscalers race to build out data centers.
On Thursday, investors will get another glimpse of the health of the AI buildout when TSMC ( TSM ) reports quarterly results. Investors expect quarterly profits to rise 60%.
Investors will pay close attention to the foundry's capacity, given ASML's ( ASML ) results on Wednesday. The maker of advanced chip-making machines warned it may not be able to fully meet demand in 2027 and 2008.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

Iran must be prepared for war even as it negotiates with the U.S., the country's parliament speaker said Wednesday.
Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf said in a televised speech that his country's main concern is preventing the U.S. from attacking again. But, he added, a signed agreement with Washington is no guarantee.
"They break their promises," said Qalibaf. As a result, Iran must be prepared to fight "against a bullying enemy," and "we must truly fight courageously on the battlefield."
"That is when we will have achieved sustainable deterrence," he said. "America must be punished. America must change its behavior. It must understand that it has to come to terms with the Iranian people."
Speaking about news reports that the U.S. is considering potential strikes against Iran before the midterms in November, President Trump said Wednesday it was his opinion that "leakers should be shot."
"In the old days, we used to shoot leakers," Mr. Trump said during a campaign rally speech in Bullhead City, Arizona. "When they leak what time you're going to attack a country, and the reason you're attacking is really for defense, because you don't want them to have a weapon that can blow up millions of people in one shot."
"Now, leakers should be dealt with very, very strongly," he added. "To me, they're the scum of the earth."
The Atlantic first reported on Oct. 7 that the Pentagon was developing strike options against Iranian targets, but no final decisions had been made. The next day, the president said on Truth Social that the U.S. would not attack Iran before the midterm elections, which take place on Nov. 3.
U.S. forces destroyed an Iran-affiliated vessel in the Gulf of Oman last week, the U.S. Central Command said on Wednesday.
CENTCOM said the dhow, a generic name for an Arab sailing vessel, was conducting surveillance and targeting U.S. Navy ships. The ship's crew members were "safely removed prior to destruction of the dhow," the military command said in a social media post .
It's unclear if the crew members were taken into custody or released.
Yemen has asked the U.S. for training and intelligence support for the Yemeni armed forces and coast guard, as well as continued political, economic and humanitarian support, but their foreign minister made no mention of military support in a briefing to reporters Wednesday.
Afrah Alzouba, Yemen's first female foreign minister, spoke in a briefing on several topics related to the ongoing Yemen-Houthi war, but did not explicitly mention requests for military support. In addition to intelligence and training, Alzouba requested the U.S. expand sanctions against the Houthis. She also asked for the EU and Washington to coordinate more closely on sanctions.
She struck an aggressive tone when asked about possible negotiations with the Houthi militia, saying, "We are not calling for starting any negotiations." The Yemeni government eventually wants a peaceful settlement but is prioritizing military operations to end Houthi control, she said.
She also emphasized Yemeni ownership of ongoing operations with air support from coalition partners: "The decision is Yemeni. The command is Yemeni. The soldiers are Yemenis."
The Saudis are the strongest backers of the official Yemeni government forces, which has earned the ire of the Houthis. They have repeatedly targeted civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, including a strike that killed 13 people at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport. A four-year ceasefire between the two sides fell apart this summer.
Alzouba said the contacts cited last month by President Trump between the U.S. and Houthis, which surprised some in the U.S., involved "warnings" against further attacks. She did not elaborate on timing or channels.
The head of Britain's top domestic spy agency MI5, Sir Ken McCallum, painted a dark picture Tuesday of the changing national security threats facing the U.K. and the world.
"We have entered a new era of national security, requiring a new response," he said in his annual threat update at MI5 headquarters in London. "Those who mean the U.K. harm aren't attacking things government owns or controls. … They're aiming at people, businesses, communities."
Iran has used and continues "using criminal proxies to try to intimidate oppositionists, Iranian media organizations, and Israeli sites," McCallum said.
But analysts have also seen "Iran, like Russia, attempting to expand their hybrid campaign," he said, leading to more than 50 arrests in the U.K. over the last year alone.
"Sadly, much of this aggression has been aimed at British Jewish communities," McCallum said, speaking of incidents this year that included "a wave of arson and sabotage incidents targeting Jewish communities in the U.K. and other European nations," but also acts targeting "harder targets, like military sites."
At least 10 vessels have been attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz since Sunday, a high since war broke out between the United States, Israel and Iran, security data showed Wednesday.
Four vessels were struck on Tuesday and six on Sunday — the highest number of attacks in a single day since the start of the conflict — according to data from security firm Vanguard, the International Maritime Organization and the British maritime agency UKMTO.
Two seafarers have been reported missing and a container ship reportedly sank as a result of recent attacks, according to the maritime sources.
Merchant vessels transiting the vital passage were first targeted by Iran in March in retaliation for U.S.-Israeli strikes on its territory, and Tehran has continued to strike vessels passing through the strait via routes it has not approved.
The attacks have disrupted shipping through the strait, which is normally one of the busiest routes for exporting oil and other commodities from Gulf countries.
Twenty-three attacks have been recorded since the start of October, almost double the average monthly number of incidents since the start of the war.
"Gulf oil flows have been recovering, with traffic through Hormuz recently returning to around 80 percent of pre-war levels despite the conflict," Vanguard analyst Barun Gupta told AFP on Wednesday.
"Increasing the tempo of attacks therefore gives Tehran a way of demonstrating that it can still disrupt that recovery and impose costs on commercial shipping and global energy markets," Gupta continued.
The Yemeni government has spoken with Beijing about the Houthis' alleged attempts to utilize Chinese-made technology for weapons, a Yemeni minister said on Wednesday.
"The Chinese are partners and we have discussed with them about, you know, the use of dual products," Foreign Minister Afrah al-Zouba said in response to an AFP question about reports the Iran-backed group was trying to secure Chinese components to help manufacture weapons.
"They were very keen for any sort of information so they can investigate it. Their support to the Yemeni government is clear," Zouba added.
The minister spoke to journalists via a virtual press conference to address the war in Yemen, which has also drawn in the government's main backer, Saudi Arabia.
The comments came after a recent report by the Conflict Armament Research group alleged the Houthis were attempting to produce advanced medium-range ballistic missiles.
Conflict Armament Research also suggested the group was "expanding its supply chains beyond Iran-linked supply networks, with several purpose-built missile components found alongside shipping documents that listed a Chinese supplier."
The escalating war between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces is cutting off lifesaving food supplies to about 800,000 people in the region, according to the U.N. World Food Programme .

articles.title_orig: Ancient shipwreck discovered off Turkey claimed to be world’s oldest
articles.title_zh: Ancient shipwreck discovered off Turkey claimed to be world’s oldest
articles.content_orig:
By XANTHA LEATHAM, EXECUTIVE SCIENCE EDITOR
Published: 08:28 EDT, 14 October 2026 | Updated: 15:35 EDT, 14 October 2026
Having sunk to the bottom of the sea when the pyramids were being built, its treasures could have been lost to the sands of time.
But a wave of luck has swept over archeologists after they discovered what is believed to be the world's oldest known shipwreck off Turkey's coast - dating back an astonishing 4,700 years.
The vessel was found near Kekova Island in Antalya and is thought to have sunk between 2600 BC and 2400 BC, around the same time the Great Pyramid of Giza was being built.
Although the ship's wooden hull has long since decayed, divers uncovered a cargo of ancient storage pots and stone anchors resting nearly 100ft (30m) below the surface.
Researchers say the discovery predates the famous Dokos wreck in Greece , previously regarded as the world's oldest known shipwreck.
The archaeologists who found the ship say it was about 32ft (10m) in length and was a trade vessel carrying cargo.
‘The shipwreck is a time capsule at the bottom of the sea,’ Professor Hakan Oniz, from Akdeniz University in Turkey, who led the Mediterranean Archaeology Association expedition, said.
Although the ship's wooden hull has long since decayed, divers uncovered a cargo of ancient storage pots and stone anchors resting nearly 100ft (30m) below the surface
More than 30 ceramic pots called amphorae were identified, along with three stone anchors
The newly identified wreck lies in an area of the Mediterranean that contains several ancient shipwrecks from different periods, including Roman vessels
In total, more than 30 ceramic pots called amphorae were identified at the site, along with three stone anchors.
Experts believe the vessel was a trading ship carrying goods such as olive oil or wine across the eastern Mediterranean.
Analysis of the clay suggests the amphorae were probably produced in workshops in the Jordan Valley before being transported by sea.
Similar vessels have previously been found near the Egyptian pyramids at Giza, Saqqara and Abusir, as well as at Troy and on Crete, hinting at extensive Bronze Age trade networks.
According to the researchers, the ship may have departed from a port on the Levantine coast and been sailing west towards Troy or Crete when disaster struck.
In their study published in the Journal of Maritime Archaeology , the team wrote: ‘Current information suggests that the shipwreck is from a small vessel that sank while sailing east to west during the Early Bronze Age.’
Analysis of the clay suggests the amphorae were probably produced in workshops in the Jordan Valley before being transported by sea
According to the researchers, the ship may have departed from a port on the Levantine coast and been sailing west towards Troy or Crete when disaster struck
Experts believe the vessel was a trading ship carrying goods such as olive oil or wine across the eastern Mediterranean
Experts described the find as a 'time capsule at the bottom of the sea'. Their discovery suggests sailors may have produced their own food during voyages
Are you amazed by the discovery of what could be the world's oldest known shipwreck? What other secrets do you think might be waiting beneath the sea?
Turkey's Culture and Tourism Minister, Mehmet Nuri Ersoy, hailed the find as evidence of the world's oldest shipwreck and said it sheds new light on Anatolia's maritime past.
‘We are bringing to light the traces of the world’s oldest shipwreck,’ he said.
‘Clay analyses indicate that the amphorae were probably produced in workshops in the Jordan Valley.
‘The discovery of similar examples in Egypt, Troy and Crete is of great importance for understanding the trade networks that connected different regions by sea.’
He added: ‘Among the finds, one amphora stands out, featuring nine different markings and two holes in its body.
‘Thought to have possibly been used as a churn in cheese or butter production, this vessel offers clues that sailors may have produced their own food during long voyages.’

articles.title_orig: Supreme Court again sides with Trump in campaign ad dispute
articles.title_zh: Supreme Court again sides with Trump in campaign ad dispute
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON, Oct 14 (Reuters) - The US Supreme Court again sided with Republicans on Wednesday in the latest clash over a new Federal Communications Commission policy that gives party committees access to discounted TV and radio advertising rates long available to political candidates.
The court agreed to ‌let the FCC, which is chaired by Trump ally Brendan Carr, avoid a judicially imposed deadline that would have forced the agency to rule ‌on a Democratic challenge to the policy before the November 3 midterm elections. The FCC joined two Republican committees in filing a request to the Supreme Court to lift the lower court's deadline.
The court ​has a 6-3 conservative majority. Liberal Justices Sonia Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson indicated they would have denied the request.
The FCC, which currently has a 2-1 Republican majority, modified its so-called "lowest unit charge" rule in March in a move seen as a boost to President Donald Trump's fellow Republicans. The president's party is seeking to retain control of Congress in the November 3 midterms.
"We are pleased the Supreme Court has granted the FCC's stay request. The court's decision is right on the law and avoids the specter of upending ‌the rules for political ads right in the middle of ⁠an ongoing election," an FCC spokesperson said.
Chief Justice John Roberts had previously lifted the October 9 deadline that was given to the FCC by the Richmond-based 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals. The 4th Circuit has accused the FCC of repeated "delay tactics" in ⁠the case, and emphasized the need for an urgent ruling in the Democratic challenge given the looming election.
The Supreme Court's latest action marks the second time in recent weeks that it has addressed the FCC's policy, as major Republican committees head toward the midterms with a cash advantage over their Democratic counterparts.
In September, the court granted a request by the national Republican ​committees ​that support the party's candidates in Senate and House of Representatives races to revive the policy ​after the 4th Circuit blocked it. The justices in an ‌8-1 ruling said that the Democratic candidates must wait for the FCC to rule before filing a challenge in court.
The FCC policy at issue requires broadcasters to charge discounted rates for airing certain political advertisements within 60 days of a general election, a window that opened this year on September 4.
A group of Democratic candidates including Senator Jon Ossoff of Georgia in April challenged the policy through in-house proceedings at the FCC. When the agency took no action, the Democrats successfully challenged the policy in the 4th Circuit, a ruling that was later halted by the Supreme Court.
The 4th Circuit on October 7 ordered the FCC to issue a prompt ruling on the ‌Democratic in-house challenge, more than five months after it was filed. In its 2-1 ruling, the ​4th Circuit said its "willingness to tolerate the FCC's delay tactics is at an end."
The Republican committees ​in their Supreme Court filing accused the 4th Circuit of having "short-circuited" the ​FCC's review process.
The Democratic candidates, for their part, accused the FCC in court papers of engaging in "blatant procedural trench warfare to stave ‌off judicial review of an unlawful agency directive until it is ​too late to matter."
The FCC policy gained ​greater significance after the Supreme Court in June struck down federal restrictions on spending coordinated between parties and their candidates, siding with Republican challengers including Vice President JD Vance. Since the June ruling, Republican committees have blown past the former limits ahead of the midterms.
The two Republican committees have exceeded the ​former national caps by more than $48 million, according to Federal ‌Election Commission spending disclosures for July and August. Their Democratic counterparts also eclipsed the former limits, but by much less — just under $4 million.
The three ​main national Republican committees ended August with about $233 million in cash. Their Democratic counterparts held roughly $130 million but also carried nearly $18 million in ​debt, according to Federal Election Commission filings.
(Reporting by John Kruzel; Editing by Will Dunham)

articles.title_orig: Trump says leakers should be shot: ‘They’re the scum of the earth’
articles.title_zh: Trump says leakers should be shot: ‘They’re the scum of the earth’
articles.content_orig:
United States President Donald Trump has suggested that those who leak information to the news media should be shot as punishment.
Trump made the remarks at a campaign rally in Bullhead City, Arizona, as he urged supporters to vote in the November 3 midterm elections.
“In my opinion, leakers should be shot,” Trump told the crowd. “In the old days, we used to shoot leakers, you know, when they leak what time you’re going to attack a country.”
Trump made the statement in an apparent reference to Operation Midnight Hammer, which saw the US launch a surprise attack on Iran in June 2025 during the 12-day war between Israel and Iran.
In the aftermath of the attack, several media outlets published findings from a preliminary report by the US Defense Intelligence Agency.
That report – which had not yet been released to the public – indicated that Iran was able to move some of its enriched uranium away from the sites the US had bombed.
It also suggested that the extent of the damage to Iran’s nuclear facilities was more modest than what Trump had asserted.
Trump, however, appeared to signal that the timing of the US attacks was among the leaked information. He accused the news media of putting military members in danger, calling out The New York Times and CNN in particular.
“They leaked the time we were leaving, the time we were arriving,” Trump said, claiming he had to reschedule the bombing campaign two days later as a result.
“Somebody leaked. Some sleaze-bag, they ought to go to jail or be shot. For the rest of their life, they should be in jail.”
Trump has long had an adversarial relationship with the news media, and he has previously called for harsh punishment against any official who passes on confidential information to news outlets.
After parts of the Defense Intelligence Agency report became public, he blamed lawmakers in the Democratic Party for its release.
“The Democrats are the ones who leaked the information on the PERFECT FLIGHT to the Nuclear Sites in Iran,” Trump wrote on social media at the time. “They should be prosecuted!”
Under Trump, the White House has taken aggressive action to track down the source of leaks.
Staff in his administration , as well as officers in the military, have also been asked to take polygraph tests.
Journalists at several news outlets, including The New York Times, The Washington Post and The Wall Street Journal, have also received subpoenas aimed at determining the sources of internal information made public.
The newspapers had reported on stories such as a botched Navy SEALs raid in North Korea and how Trump ignored internal Pentagon warnings against launching the Iran war.
Last year, the Department of Defense demanded that journalists who wished to access the Pentagon sign an agreement not to publish unauthorised material.
Much of the Pentagon press corps refused to agree, and a federal court struck down many of the new demands made on journalists at the department.
Trump has long raged against leakers, going back to his first term as president from 2017 to 2021.
Former White House official Alyssa Farah Griffin told a podcast in 2024 that Trump had called for leakers to be executed, after media outlets reported that he had taken shelter in a White House bunker during racial justice protests in 2020.
Trump appeared to reprise that sentiment in his speech to Arizona voters on Wednesday, less than three weeks before the November 3 midterms.
“Leakers should be dealt with very, very strongly,” Trump said. “To me, they are the scum of the earth.”

articles.title_orig: 'It wasn't supposed to end like this': Woman kills husband, son at Great Wolf Lodge, police say
articles.title_zh: 'It wasn't supposed to end like this': Woman kills husband, son at Great Wolf Lodge, police say
articles.content_orig:
A Bradford County woman is accused of killing her husband and her 3-year-old son inside a guest room at the Great Wolf Lodge in Monroe County.
Metallica Harrison , 27, of Towanda, was charged with two counts of criminal homicide in the deaths of her husband, Charles Harrison , and her son, whose name has not yet been released.
According to the affidavit of probable cause, Pocono Township police officers responded to a Great Wolf Lodge room around 3:13 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 12, after Metallica called the Monroe County Control Center.
Police said Metallica told the 911 dispatcher that she needed "help dying" and was "unable to find a vein in her neck to stab."
Officers encountered Metallica in the room's doorway and saw her wrist bleeding and superficial puncture wounds around her neck, according to the affidavit. Investigators said Metallica told officers that "she wanted to be with her husband and son."
Officers entered the room while checking on Metallica's family and found Charles and her son dead on separate mattresses on the floor, according to investigators.
Police said Charles had suffered multiple stab wounds to the chest. The child appeared to have suffered one stab wound to the chest, according to authorities.
Investigators reviewed the recording of Metallica's call to 911. According to the affidavit, Metallica told the dispatcher, "I'm too weak to stab my neck" and "I need police."
When the dispatcher asked whether she had any weapons, Metallica said she had knives and added, "That's what I've been using, and it's not working," according to the documents.
When asked whether she was alone, Metallica responded, "My husband and son are already gone in the bed in the living room," the affidavit stated. "They're already gone. I'm sorry," she later said.
Investigators said Metallica  did not request assistance for her husband or son at any point during the call.
According to police, Metallica was transported to St. Luke's Hospital–Monroe Campus in Stroudsburg for treatment of her injuries. A Pocono Township police officer accompanied her during the transport.
During the ambulance ride, police said Metallica stated several times that she was "not supposed to be here." According to the affidavit, Metallica  said, "I f----- up, I f----- up. I just needed energy and strength."
Investigators said that Metallica questioned why there was not "an easier way" and asked emergency medical personnel how deep the vein in her wrist was so she would know "for next time." According to police, Metallica also stated she had taken medication to thin her blood and expressed frustration that her blood was clotting.
"Every day, I work so hard. To be the best person, the best mother, the best wife," Metallica said, according to the affidavit. "It wasn't supposed to end like this. I was supposed to have my happy family. That's what I envisioned since I was a child," the documents stated.
Video below: Metallica Harrison accused of killing husband, son
According to investigators, a large butcher knife was found on the bathroom floor and a smaller knife was found on the bathroom sink. Police said both knives had teal-green handles. Great Wolf Lodge employees told investigators that the knives were not the type maintained by the resort, according to the affidavit.
Police also reported finding several medication bottles throughout the room. Investigators said a plastic container on the floor and a garbage can in the bathroom held a brownish-red liquid believed to be blood.
Great Wolf Lodge security personnel told investigators that Charles, Metallica and the 3-year-old checked into the resort on Sept. 21. The family extended its reservation Oct. 5 and was scheduled to check out Oct. 13, according to the affidavit.
Police reviewed surveillance video that showed the entire family entering the room at 6:53 p.m. on Oct. 11, according to investigators. At approximately 8:12 p.m., Metallica left the room and used a microwave in a vending area and returned at 8:16 p.m., the affidavit stated.
Metallica and Charles left the room at approximately 10:43 p.m., went to the resort's arcade and returned at approximately 11:22 p.m., according to investigators.
Police said the surveillance review showed no additional activity at the room's door after the couple returned from the arcade.
Police said search warrants were obtained for the hotel, Metallica and Charles's vehicle, which was parked in the resort's lot.
Investigators met with Metallica at the hospital, advised her of her Miranda rights and asked what had led to her hospitalization, according to officials. Police said Metallica responded that she was "suicidal, not stupid" and declined to speak with them.
Detectives said they collected a buccal swab for DNA testing.
Authorities noted that other than the lacerations to her left wrist and a puncture wound to her neck, Metallica had no other injuries, bruising or apparent defensive wounds.
Police said based on the evidence, Metallica was charged with two counts of criminal homicide, and awaits arraignment.
The Pocono Township Police Department said the investigation remains active.
The department described the case as "an isolated domestic tragedy" and said there was no threat to the community.
"Our thoughts and deepest condolences go out to the family and loved ones affected by this tragedy," Pocono Township Police said.
Great Wolf Resorts shared the following statement with WGAL, saying:
"We are deeply saddened and heartbroken by a tragic domestic incident that occurred yesterday in a guest room at our resort in the Pocono Mountains.  It was an isolated family incident, and we’re cooperating fully with local law enforcement as they conduct their investigation.  Our thoughts are with the family and loved ones of those affected.
"Out of respect for those involved, as well as the integrity of the investigation, we ask that any further information regarding this matter be directed to Pocono Township Police Department.
"I can tell you law enforcement assessed the situation yesterday, determined it was isolated family incident and verified there was no ongoing security concerns."
If you or someone you know is struggling with suicidal thoughts or mental health matters, please call the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 (or 1-800-273-8255 ) to connect with a trained counselor. You can also text TALK to 741741.
Great Wolf Lodge operates more than 20 family-oriented resorts across North America featuring indoor water parks maintained at 84 degrees year-round. Its properties offer lodging, dining, children's activities and other attractions.
The Pocono Mountains location opened in October 2005 as the company's sixth resort and is about 90 minutes west of New York City and two hours north of Philadelphia.

articles.title_orig: Hegseth calls US$1.5 trillion defence budget ‘critical’ to counter China
articles.title_zh: Hegseth calls US$1.5 trillion defence budget ‘critical’ to counter China
articles.content_orig:
Pentagon chief warns US risks falling behind China in drones, robotics and AI without major investment in military capabilities
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has called a nearly US$1.5 trillion defence budget request “absolutely critical”, warning that whoever falls behind in autonomy, robotics and AI will fall “even further behind” as Washington eyes China’s rapid military modernisation.
Speaking at a panel discussion during the Association of the United States Army (AUSA) Annual Meeting and Exposition on Wednesday, Hegseth said that Project Agincourt, the Pentagon’s initiative to accelerate drone and autonomous warfare capabilities, is the “end state” of what the administration has focused on since “day one”.
Asked how significant the increase to nearly US$1.5 trillion in the defence budget is, Hegseth replied that it is “absolutely critical” and a “one-time generational investment” that gives Washington a chance to “fully rebuild” the military amid threats from adversaries.

articles.title_orig: Measles cases surge past 150 in Kentucky; big outbreak identified in one county
articles.title_zh: Measles cases surge past 150 in Kentucky; big outbreak identified in one county
articles.content_orig:
Just days after Kentucky's measles case count hit 100, dozens more have been reported.
As of Wednesday, the number of cases reported in the Commonwealth is now 157 for 2026.
Most of those come out of Laurel County, which had seven cases just a few days ago. Now, it has 56, according to the state's dashboard .
Laurel County is in southeast Kentucky,
The dashboard says that outbreak involves people who are unvaccinated from several large households that have been "isolated from the broader community."
In only one case did the person report having the full vaccine. One case had one MMR dose, and the rest didn't have any.
Of the total state count, nine of those cases have led to hospitalization.
So far, no deaths have been reported.
There were only 13 cases overall in 2025, and none were reported the year prior.
Measles is a disease caused by a highly contagious virus.
It is spread through the air when someone with measles sneezes, coughs, or breathes.
Symptoms include high fever, cough, runny nose, red and watery eyes, and rash. Tiny white spots can appear inside the mouth two to three days after symptoms begin.
The disease can be especially severe in infants, pregnant women, and people who have weakened immune systems.
While rare, measles can result in death.
Kentucky health officials have warned this is the highest case count in decades. Dr. Steve Stack, with the Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services, along with other local health officials, has been encouraging people to get vaccinated.
"We do not need to have measles," Gov. Andy Beshear said last month. "We have a proven tool that for over a quarter century eliminated it from the United States. The only reason it's resurging now is because of, I think, negligent information and guidance being shared freely. We want people to not feel vilified or maligned. We want people to feel informed."

articles.title_orig: Mike Tomlin’s Minecraft World Is the Talk of the Internet, but How Good Is It Really?
articles.title_zh: Mike Tomlin’s Minecraft World Is the Talk of the Internet, but How Good Is It Really?
articles.content_orig:
Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.
Football coaches have the freedom to create their own worlds on the playing field. But retired Steelers legend Mike Tomlin took a different route — manifesting his vision block by block within a massive Minecraft city. What started as a shared family project with his children evolved into a solitary, 12-year labor of love. Now, the sheer depth of Tomlin’s digital city is capturing widespread attention online.
Tomlin served as the Steelers’ head coach for 19 seasons before resigning in January, having never finished with a losing record.
His video was released Oct. 1 and received more than 3 million views in less than two weeks. In the video, Tomlin shows off an expansive Minecraft city, complete with sports stadiums, high-rise apartments, homes and other buildings. He began working on the city about 12 years ago after watching his kids and their friends play Minecraft when they were in middle school, building it in the game’s creative mode with their help.
“I was mesmerized by what could occupy their attention for such large periods of time,” Tomlin says in the video. “I’m certainly not skilled enough in video game play or have the stick control to [play the game’s survival mode], so I got interested in this creative mode. I like to build, I’ve always had an interest in architecture, and so I started doing this creative city as a means to spend time with them.”
His kids eventually outgrew the game and moved on to different ones, high school and eventually college. That left Tomlin to work on the city by himself, which he did off and on for years while still coaching the Steelers.
“More than anything, it was therapeutic for me, some mindless entertainment,” Tomlin says. “I’m not a big TV watcher. It allowed me to detach from the realities and pressures of life.”
Tomlin spends the rest of the video showing viewers around the place, focusing on his basic, early-days architecture, penthouses, apartments and how he tried to design a solid urban space. He plans to release more videos to discuss different buildings, the city’s design and other elements of his sprawling city.
Leading up to the video’s release, there was no indication whatsoever that Mike Tomlin played computer games. That helped make his big Minecraft debut all the more delightful. The 54-year-old coach showed off thousands of hours of playtime in a 19-minute video, and no one could believe it.
“12 years of Minecraft? Didn’t you know this? Did nobody know this?” asked a shocked Ty Schmidt, producer and on-air personality of the Pat McAfee show, on an episode of the show.
The sports world finally saw what some Minecraft fans already knew: Tomlin’s dedication to the game is unmatched.
“We’re talking block by block,” McAfee said. “He had 14 30-story buildings around a body of water that he wanted to build his city around — one block at a time! They all got patios! He had a penthouse with a shark aquarium. It was unbelievable.”
Minecraft fans, too, showed up to explore the coach’s dazzling feat. Many were surprised to learn that he built this on the Bedrock edition of the game using a video game console, beginning with PlayStation 3 before moving on to PlayStation 4 and 5. That means Tomlin didn’t have access to the mods that many builders use in the Java version of the game on PC, or the freedom that a mouse and keyboard provide. He built his city one brick at a time on a PlayStation controller.
Tomlin was initially unaware of his viral fame. In an interview on Late Night with Seth Meyers, Tomlin said he was at a gala with his phone off when the video went live, and it wasn’t until later that his kids told him about the massive response. Tomlin had caught up by the time he appeared on Football Night in America with NBC on Sunday night.
“I’m appreciating all of this, to be quite honest with you,” Tomlin said during the broadcast.
The spectacle of Tomlin’s Minecraft city is one of those wholesome events that had viewers smiling all weekend, except a few Steelers fans who were probably already pretty mad about losing to the Cleveland Browns less than 24 hours after the video was released. That didn’t stop a lot of people from wondering whether Tomlin’s city is actually as good as it looks. It turns out that most of the Internet agrees that it lives up to the hype.
“From my understanding, [it’s a] phenomenal Minecraft city,” McAfee said. “Like, as I was watching it, I was like, man, the attention to detail [is outstanding].”
Noted Minecraft city builder Alpine1 was one of the first to create his own video on the topic, and he was impressed. He had some suggestions for Tomlin, recommending that the coach consider using glass panes instead of glass blocks and more sophisticated floor designs, such as installing tile floors in showers. But Alpine1 did note that Tomlin likely started building the city before many modern building tools were available to Minecraft players.
“This is really awesome to see,” Alpine1 said in the video. “I’ve been advocating for people to build Minecraft cities for years because there’s so much you can do… and I think Mike has really captured this.”
Zach Nagel, an architecture student from the University of Cincinnati’s School of Architecture and Interior Design, also took a stab at analyzing Tomlin’s city in a separate video . He noted that Tomlin used some concepts that are actually practiced in architecture, specifically adding a penthouse with an aquarium right across the street from a full-sized aquarium.
“Now, what Coach Tomlin is talking about here, having a central theme to the building, is a term that we use in architecture as well, the parti ,” Nagel says. “If you talk to 20 architects and ask them to give a definition of a parti, you might get 20 pretty different answers. At its [simplest], a parti is a single idea or scheme that drives all of the decisions you make in a building.”
Nagel goes on to praise Tomlin for not only considering the building’s exterior appearance but also its interior design and the functional needs of the city’s fictional residents. He says that a lot of Tomlin’s design choices and approach are in line with what some architects use.
“In another world, he could’ve totally gone down this career path had he wanted to,” Nagel says. “And I’m glad to see that Minecraft remains such an accessible tool for those who want to shape the environment around them.”

articles.title_orig: UK threatens to ban Eritreans over migrant return policy
articles.title_zh: UK threatens to ban Eritreans over migrant return policy
articles.content_orig:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has threatened to ban all Eritreans from entering the UK if the east African country's government does not accept more returns of small boat migrants and foreign national offenders.
From Thursday, Eritrean diplomats will face restrictions on their movement outside London. Fast-track visas will also be stopped for VIPs.
Ministers have previously pressured other countries into accepting returns by threatening visa bans.
Eritreans were the most common nationality among small boats migrants in the 12 months to June - accounting for 18% of arrivals , according to figures from the House of Commons Library.
The Eritrean embassy in London has been contacted for comment.
"Eritrea has had every chance to accept the return of criminals and those with no right to be in the UK. Unlike other countries, it has refused," said Mahmood.
She said she would not hesitate "to impose further measures on other countries refusing to co-operate".
The UK government accused the Eritrean authorities of "abruptly" withdrawing co-operation earlier this year.
The restrictions mean diplomats are banned from travelling 60km outside London without permission.
The Home Office said this mirrored restrictions on British officials in Eritrea's capital Asmara.
Earlier this year, the UK threatened bans against Angola, Namibia and the Democratic Republic of  Congo (DRC).
Restrictions were announced against the DRC last year, but the Home Office said these have been lifted after co-operation on returns improved.
Angola and Namibia both agreed changes before restrictions were introduced.
When announcing changes to the UK's asylum system in November, Mahmood said visa penalties would be applied to countries that failed to co-operate with returns policies.
Penalties included an "emergency brake" on visas for countries with high asylum claims until they take back citizens in the UK illegally.
According to Home Office data, more than 20,400 people have arrived in the UK by small boats so far since the beginning of this year, down 40% from the same period last year.
There were more than 40,600 returns and deportations from the UK from July 2025 to June this year - an 8% increase on the same period last year.
Of those who had been returned, less than 6,000 has been convicted of a criminal offence.

articles.title_orig: Epic says its new vibe-coded Epic Games Launcher is faster than Steam
articles.title_zh: Epic says its new vibe-coded Epic Games Launcher is faster than Steam
articles.content_orig:
Nearly eight years after Epic took on Steam with its own Game Store and launcher, the Fortnite maker is deploying a new tool to give it an edge over Valve: vibe coding.
In announcing the new publicly available “Preview” build of its Epic Games Launcher, Epic writes that “programming is hard. So, instead of doing that, we vibe coded a new Epic Games Launcher that’s way faster and more responsive than the current one, and has a new look.” And while that might sound a little tongue-in-cheek, Epic Games Store General Manager and VP Martin Keely told PC Gamer that the team “started from scratch” and used AI as “a tool to write and review new features and new capabilities from the ground up in a different tech stack than what we had previously.” The goal, Keely said, was to “look at functionality that existed [in the current Epic Games Launcher] and [say] we want to replicate that, but not the code itself.”
Speaking to IGN , Keely clarified that using AI to code the new Launcher “made us more efficient and allowed a small team to rewrite the code base and be able to launch it faster across platforms, support Windows and Mac, and we’re going to have a Linux version as well.”
We vibe coded the Epic Games Launcher to be faster than the other guy.
Don’t believe us? Test it out for yourself in Preview: https://t.co/pdtAeEIri4 https://t.co/aMxojUUVPV
— Epic Games Store (@EpicGames) October 14, 2026
The focus on startup speed extends to Epic’s social media announcement , which once again stresses that “we vibe coded the Epic Games Launcher to be faster than the other guy.” Ars’s own testing confirms that the new Launcher goes from a cold start to the store page a few seconds faster than Steam (assuming no login or update issues get in the way). Epic also claims the new Launcher can restore from the system tray to the Library screen slightly faster than Steam, though the claimed difference of 0.06 seconds in this seems so small as to be unnoticeable (and was in our testing).
Epic announced a ground-up “storefront rearchitecture” and “Launcher V2 private Beta” in an Unreal Fest presentation in June . At the time, the company said the new Launcher would have “5x faster cold start” times and help solve challenges that “every developer in this room and every player” has experienced with the current Launcher.
The term “vibe coding” still carries heavy connotations of quickly thrown-together slop that could hide crucial errors beneath the surface. On social media, Epic warns that its Launcher Preview “will have some bugs” that early testers can help squash with a feedback form. The announcement post also warns that the vibe-coded Preview is currently “light on features”— an FAQ clarifies that “certain social features and account management options” haven’t made it over from the legacy version just yet.
That said, the new Preview launcher adds some long-requested features like a Recent Games list and a centralized downloads hub for tracking network activity. And Epic writes that it is “working toward feature parity” between the new Launcher and the old one.
Epic’s release of the new “vibe coded” Launcher preview comes just days after a Bloomberg report suggesting the company is pivoting to an “AI first” development model for an upcoming Star Wars and Marvel-themed shooter. “We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration,” Epic CEO Tim Sweeney wrote on social media on Monday. “The aim isn’t to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal.”

articles.title_orig: Yemen's Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities after Aramco HQ hit
articles.title_zh: Yemen's Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities after Aramco HQ hit
articles.content_orig:
“Prices aren’t going to fall anytime soon,” David Goldwyn, a former State Department special envoy and coordinator for international energy affairs, told MS NOW.
A former U.S. energy official predicted that “things are about to get worse” for Americans at the pump, after Iran-backed Houthi rebels attacked the headquarters of the Saudi-owned oil giant Aramco late Tuesday.
David Goldwyn, who served as the State Department’s special envoy and coordinator for international energy affairs during the Obama administration, told MS NOW’s Stephanie Ruhle he believes “prices aren’t going to fall anytime soon.”
Goldwyn, who now serves as the chair of the Atlantic Council Global Energy Center’s Energy Advisory Group, said the attack, which preceded a rise in oil prices Wednesday morning, “raises the question of what’s next” and listed several targets Iran and its proxies may have in their sights: “Are they going to hit OAPEC, which processes 7 million barrels a day of oil for Saudi Arabia? Are they going to hit the East-West pipeline again? Are they going to hit the terminals in Yanbu or elsewhere?”
According to Goldwyn, the strike’s timing proves that “the Iranians, in particular, clearly want to influence the U.S. midterm elections.”
The former energy official said the “risk profile is rising” in the region and there will be “increased pressure on the administration” to act. However, he said he did not think it was likely that a deal between the U.S. and Iran would be reached in the near future.
“These are the three scenarios: There’s escalation, status quo or some sort of a peace deal,” Goldwyn explained. “There’s no peace deal on the table with Iran. They clearly don’t even want to negotiate until after the midterms.” As a result, he said, “We’re looking at escalation either by the United States after the midterms or by the Iranians and the Houthis right now.”
Goldwyn also discussed Donald Trump ’s new deal with Russia, which would lift sanctions and allow the U.S. to import diesel from Russia. “It’s not going to lower prices,” he said of the agreement. “It’s not going to affect the global market. It’s putting pressure on the Ukrainians, and it’s not doing anything with the Russians.”
“Prices aren’t going to fall anytime soon,” Goldwyn added.
You can watch Goldwyn’s full comments in the clip at the top of the page.

articles.title_orig: World Championships U7–U17 2026: Young talents make their mark in Spain – International Chess Federation
articles.title_zh: World Championships U7–U17 2026: Young talents make their mark in Spain – International Chess Federation
articles.content_orig:
Surprises and perfect scores shape the opening rounds of the 2026 World Championships U7–U17
With an outstanding turnout of 721 players representing 82 countries, the 2026 FIDE World Championships U7–U17 got underway on October 13 in the coastal town of Roquetas de Mar, in the province of Almería, southern Spain.
Running until October 21, the event is jointly organized by the International Chess Federation (FIDE) and the Spanish Chess Federation and is being held at the Evenia Zoraida Beach Resort . The competition features 12 age categories: Under 7, Under 9, Under 11, Under 13, Under 15 and Under 17, with separate Open and Girls sections in each age group.
Many national delegations are represented across all six age groups, highlighting the breadth of participation at this year’s championships. Kazakhstan, for example, has players competing in every age category, underlining the importance of the event as a platform for developing young chess talent.
As is customary in tournaments of this kind, the championships follow an 11-round Swiss system. The main innovation this year is the time control: each player receives 45 minutes for the entire game, with a 30-second increment per move from move one.
Following several successful pilot events, this *fast classical* format is being introduced for the first time in an official youth championship, with all games counting towards FIDE ratings. The new time control aims to offer a more dynamic playing experience while retaining the strategic depth of classical chess.
Representing FIDE, Ozgur Solakoglu (Technical Delegate), officially opened the championships, welcoming all participants and wishing them every success and an enjoyable competition.
Javier Ochoa de Echagüen , president of the Spanish Chess Federation, acknowledged that many players had travelled long distances to take part in the event. He expressed his hope that they would enjoy their stay at the resort and perform to the best of their abilities over the coming days.
Finally, International Arbiter Panagiotis Nikolopoulos reviewed some of the main rules and regulations and reminded players of the tournament schedule. With the formalities completed, he started the clocks for the first of the two rounds scheduled for the opening day.
As is customary in Swiss-system tournaments, where the top seeds are generally paired against lower-rated opponents in the early rounds, most of the favourites made a strong start. However, there were a few surprises, particularly in the youngest age groups.
The Under 7 Open section is especially unpredictable, with more than half of the participants yet to receive a FIDE rating. With so many players still establishing their competitive strength, the opening rounds offer plenty of scope for unexpected results and emerging talents to make their mark.
Under 7 (53 players in the open section and 28 players in the girls’ section)
The youngest participants play in a dedicated room adapted to their needs, with a spacious waiting area nearby where parents can easily collect their children as soon as their games finish.
After two rounds, the top two seeds in the Under 7 Open section, Spain’s Pau Vizcaya Lopez and Egypt’s Mohab Ahmed Assem , are among a group of 10 players who have won both their games and share the lead with a perfect 2/2 score.
In the Girls’ section, five players have also won both games. Uzbekistan’s Malika Ikromova tops the standings on tiebreak.
Under 9 (82 players in the open section and 40 players in the girls’ section)
In the Girls’ section, second seed Varvara Volkova , competing under the FIDE flag, holds the top position on tiebreak. Five other players have also won their first two games, including Finland’s Stella Zhu , the highest-rated participant in the field.
In the Open section, 14 players share the lead with a perfect score after two rounds, headed by Latvia’s Akims Jefimovs . Top seed Wiktor Stankowski of Poland has already dropped half a point and sits just behind the leaders.
Under 11 (99 players in the open section and 47 players in the girls’ section)
Candidate Master Amirzhan Anetov leads the Under 11 Open section after winning both of his games, with 14 other players close behind on a perfect score. Seeds two to five have all dropped points, underlining the strength of the field and suggesting that several young competitors may be underrated.
In the Girls’ section, only six players have maintained a perfect score after two rounds. Israel’s Arbel Ben Ari is the surprise leader on tiebreak, despite being ranked just 43rd among the 47 participants at the start of the tournament.
Under 13 (75 players in the open section and 43 players in the girls’ section)
WFM Alina Donets , representing Austria, leads the Under 13 Girls’ section on tiebreak, although she shares a perfect score with seven other players. In this category, most of the top seeds have lived up to expectations, demonstrating their strength in the early rounds.
The Under 13 Open section is even more tightly contested, with 15 players sharing the lead on 2/2. While the top seeds remain in contention, it is surprise performer Saravanan Keertieshvar , seeded 53rd, who currently tops the standings.
Unfortunately, the second and fourth seeds, both FIDE Masters representing Syria, have yet to arrive in Spain. They are expected to join the competition tomorrow, but will have to begin their campaigns from zero points after missing the opening rounds.
Under 15 (85 players in the open section and 43 players in the girls’ section)
In the Under 15 Open section, 16 players have won both their games, including the six highest-ranked masters in the category. Kazakhstan’s Zhanbolat Amankos deserves special mention after producing one of the biggest upsets of the round by defeating Austria’s FM Florentin Stickler .
In the Under 15 Girls’ section, local player Amaya Alfaro Aldunate scored an impressive second-round victory over Turkey’s WCM Arya Aydogan. She is among nine players who have started the tournament with two wins from two games. WFM Aiaru Altynbek currently leads the group on tiebreak.

China’s WIM Xue Tianhao leads the Under 17 Girls’ section on tiebreak, sharing a perfect score with eight other players. Top seed WIM Mariya Kholyavko of Kazakhstan has already dropped half a point, but with nine rounds still to play, there is plenty of time for the standings to change.
In the Open section, top seed FM Maxime Hauchamps is among 12 players who have won both their games. The opening rounds have already produced several surprises, underlining the competitive strength of the field and promising plenty of exciting chess in the days ahead.
Pre-tournament open U-17 favourite FM Maxime Hauchamps (2419) has started off very well with two consecutive wins. In his first-round game, he executed a nice tactic against Spaniard Pablo Martinez Soriano (2127).
Hauchamps has castled queenside and launched a kingside attack. Black’s knight has landed on d5, and White finds a surprising way to tactically exploit the position.
The key move is 20. Rxd5! , when White sacrifices the rook for Black’s knight, opening lines and maintaining the initiative against the king. Of course, the bishop on e7 is hanging, which forces Black’s hand.
The game continued 20…Bxg5 and now the intermediate move 21. Rc5! Hitting the queen and winning material. After 21… Qb6 Hauchamps recaptured 22. hxg5 and went on to win.

articles.title_orig: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms young users
articles.title_zh: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms young users
articles.content_orig:
Eight states filed lawsuits against OpenAI on Wednesday alleging that the artificial intelligence company's ChatGPT chatbot is an unsafe product that's harmed children and deceived parents.
Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana have individually sued OpenAI in their own state courts, Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird said in a release . She said Iowa's lawsuit aims to "vindicate the rights of Iowans affected by OpenAI's willful, dangerous, reckless, and unlawful conduct."
"OpenAI is hurting kids and they are lying to Iowans," Bird said in a statement. "OpenAI claims ChatGPT is safe while it's giving dangerous medical advice, encouraging people to hurt others, and coaching people to commit suicide — all while pretending to be their fake friend. My lawsuit is about protecting our kids and holding OpenAI accountable under our state law."
OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company has built age-specific protections into its product that "many other AI products lack." He added that OpenAI is working with states to advance policies that will apply to the entire industry.
"While no system can be perfect, we'll continue to work with experts to inform our work and build additional safeguards, such as the parental controls, break reminders and age-appropriate model protections that exist today," Pusateri said.
OpenAI is facing mounting scrutiny over its safety and security practices, including around how the company is working to protect children. In a number of wrongful death lawsuits , ChatGPT is blamed for driving users to experience harmful delusions and, in some cases, to commit suicide. Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier also sued OpenAI in June, alleging the company knowingly released an unsafe product that could harm users.
OpenAI has taken steps to enhance safety features for parents and children over the last year, and in August it launched a dedicated experience for minors called ChatGPT for Teens . That product includes a range of educational features and age-appropriate safeguards that are intended to reduce exposure to developmentally inappropriate or harmful content.
"Teens should be able to use AI to learn, create, and explore," OpenAI said in a release at the time. "But that access should come with protections that reflect their developmental stage, reinforce real-world relationships, and support healthy use over time."
If you are having suicidal thoughts or are in distress, contact the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 for support and assistance from a trained counselor.

articles.title_orig: GOP gets another Supreme Court win in TV political ad fight
articles.title_zh: GOP gets another Supreme Court win in TV political ad fight
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON, Oct 14 (Reuters) - The US Supreme Court again sided with Republicans on Wednesday in the latest clash over a new Federal Communications Commission policy that gives party committees access to discounted TV and radio advertising rates long available to political candidates.
The court agreed to ‌let the FCC, which is chaired by Trump ally Brendan Carr, avoid a judicially imposed deadline that would have forced the agency to rule ‌on a Democratic challenge to the policy before the November 3 midterm elections. The FCC joined two Republican committees in filing a request to the Supreme Court to lift the lower court's deadline.
The court ​has a 6-3 conservative majority. Liberal Justices Sonia Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson indicated they would have denied the request.
The FCC, which currently has a 2-1 Republican majority, modified its so-called "lowest unit charge" rule in March in a move seen as a boost to President Donald Trump's fellow Republicans. The president's party is seeking to retain control of Congress in the November 3 midterms.
"We are pleased the Supreme Court has granted the FCC's stay request. The court's decision is right on the law and avoids the specter of upending ‌the rules for political ads right in the middle of ⁠an ongoing election," an FCC spokesperson said.
Chief Justice John Roberts had previously lifted the October 9 deadline that was given to the FCC by the Richmond-based 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals. The 4th Circuit has accused the FCC of repeated "delay tactics" in ⁠the case, and emphasized the need for an urgent ruling in the Democratic challenge given the looming election.
The Supreme Court's latest action marks the second time in recent weeks that it has addressed the FCC's policy, as major Republican committees head toward the midterms with a cash advantage over their Democratic counterparts.
In September, the court granted a request by the national Republican ​committees ​that support the party's candidates in Senate and House of Representatives races to revive the policy ​after the 4th Circuit blocked it. The justices in an ‌8-1 ruling said that the Democratic candidates must wait for the FCC to rule before filing a challenge in court.
The FCC policy at issue requires broadcasters to charge discounted rates for airing certain political advertisements within 60 days of a general election, a window that opened this year on September 4.
A group of Democratic candidates including Senator Jon Ossoff of Georgia in April challenged the policy through in-house proceedings at the FCC. When the agency took no action, the Democrats successfully challenged the policy in the 4th Circuit, a ruling that was later halted by the Supreme Court.
The 4th Circuit on October 7 ordered the FCC to issue a prompt ruling on the ‌Democratic in-house challenge, more than five months after it was filed. In its 2-1 ruling, the ​4th Circuit said its "willingness to tolerate the FCC's delay tactics is at an end."
The Republican committees ​in their Supreme Court filing accused the 4th Circuit of having "short-circuited" the ​FCC's review process.
The Democratic candidates, for their part, accused the FCC in court papers of engaging in "blatant procedural trench warfare to stave ‌off judicial review of an unlawful agency directive until it is ​too late to matter."
The FCC policy gained ​greater significance after the Supreme Court in June struck down federal restrictions on spending coordinated between parties and their candidates, siding with Republican challengers including Vice President JD Vance. Since the June ruling, Republican committees have blown past the former limits ahead of the midterms.
The two Republican committees have exceeded the ​former national caps by more than $48 million, according to Federal ‌Election Commission spending disclosures for July and August. Their Democratic counterparts also eclipsed the former limits, but by much less — just under $4 million.
The three ​main national Republican committees ended August with about $233 million in cash. Their Democratic counterparts held roughly $130 million but also carried nearly $18 million in ​debt, according to Federal Election Commission filings.
(Reporting by John Kruzel; Editing by Will Dunham)
